answers.answer:
1. For four players select 3 random-numbered Pods: lowest number in Section A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up.
2. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults at four players) in the bag.
answers.evidence: “For four players select 3 random-numbered Pods: lowest number in Section A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up.” (Setup)

answers.answer:
1. Remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards showing a player count above the actual count; shuffle decks separately and deal each player one of each, hidden, before Character draft.
2. At the First Encounter, each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other face down from game; nobody may inspect others’ removed cards.
3. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger First Encounter/Objective choice.
answers.evidence: “Remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards showing a player count above the actual count; shuffle decks separately and deal each player one of each, hidden, before Character draft.” (Setup; First Encounter)

answers.answer:
1. Discard the used Action card plus exactly two other Action cards for its printed cost 2; with two other Action cards the payment is possible and all four Action cards leave the hand.
2. Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost.
3. Choose one of the card’s OR sections.
answers.evidence: “Discard the used Action card plus exactly two other Action cards for its printed cost 2; with two other Action cards the payment is possible and all four Action cards leave the hand.” (Actions)

answers.answer:
1. After finishing their own round, including the round in which they take one Action and pass, they suffer one Light Wound for ending in Fire.
2. After passing they cannot take further normal Actions that Player Phase, but may discard any number of hand cards when passing; FAQ permits Interruption after passing.
3. Later players’ rounds do not cause this Character another Fire wound; only their own round-end check applies.
answers.evidence: “After finishing their own round, including the round in which they take one Action and pass, they suffer one Light Wound for ending in Fire.” (Turn Structure; Fire markers)

answers.answer:
1. Enter the neighboring Room; if tile face down, flip it, set Item count by aligning token number with board Item Counter (except Nest/Slime Room), resolve its symbol, then remove token to box.
2. If destination is empty, make Noise roll unless Exploration Silence/Danger replaces it; Silence means no roll, Danger moves all eligible non-Combat neighboring Intruders in, or if none places Noise in each connected unmarked Corridor.
3. If any Character or Intruder is already in destination, do not make the ordinary Noise roll.
4. Slime marks Character, Fire/Malfunction marks Room, Doors places token in entry Corridor.
answers.evidence: “Enter the neighboring Room; if tile face down, flip it, set Item count by aligning token number with board Item Counter (except Nest/Slime Room), resolve its symbol, then remove token to box.” (Movement; Exploration tokens; Noise roll)

answers.answer:
1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with a Noise marker in a chosen connected Corridor; FAQ says it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results.
2. Cannot use in Combat or if every Corridor connected to destination already has Noise; normal Movement restrictions still apply.
3. Closed Doors block player passage; miniatures may never stop in Corridors.
answers.evidence: “Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with a Noise marker in a chosen connected Corridor; FAQ says it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results.” (Basic Actions; Movement)

answers.answer:
1. If instructed to place Noise in an already marked Corridor, resolve an Encounter instead; first discard all Noise from Room-connected Corridors, including shared Technical Corridor if applicable.
2. Draw token, place matching miniature; compare its number with triggering player’s hand counting Action and Contamination cards; fewer cards means Surprise Attack against that player. Set non-Blank drawn token aside outside bag.
3. A Technical Corridors Noise marker occupies the shared space and counts for every Technical Entrance; the usual one-marker limit applies.
answers.evidence: “If instructed to place Noise in an already marked Corridor, resolve an Encounter instead; first discard all Noise from Room-connected Corridors, including shared Technical Corridor if applicable.” (Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Encounters)

answers.answer:
1. Danger moves all Intruders in neighboring Rooms that are not in Combat with any Character into the entered Room.
2. If none, or all neighboring Intruders are in Combat, place Noise in every connected Corridor lacking a marker, including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance.
3. Mere movement of Intruder into Character Room is not an Encounter.
4. Slime makes Silence resolve as Danger.
answers.evidence: “Danger moves all Intruders in neighboring Rooms that are not in Combat with any Character into the entered Room.” (Exploration tokens; Noise roll; Encounters)

answers.answer:
1. Place Noise in every Corridor connected to Room; no miniature appears; return Blank to bag.
2. If Blank was last token in bag, add one Adult token if available, otherwise none, then return Blank.
3. Add one Adult token if any available, then return Blank; this branch does not specify Noise placement.
answers.evidence: “Place Noise in every Corridor connected to Room; no miniature appears; return Blank to bag.” (Encounters; Intruder bag development)

answers.answer:
1. Both stay in their starting Room; the Closed Door is destroyed (lay token down).
2. Destroyed Door permits movement and cannot be closed again (except Plasma Torch).
3. An Intruder appearing through a Closed Door because of Noise is not blocked; it appears regardless.
answers.evidence: “Both stay in their starting Room; the Closed Door is destroyed (lay token down).” (Doors)

answers.answer:
1. Remove miniature, discard all its Injury markers, return its token to bag; existing Noise marker on shared Technical space remains.
2. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors, except Mechanic Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans Item.
3. Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: “Remove miniature, discard all its Injury markers, return its token to bag; existing Noise marker on shared Technical space remains.” (Technical Corridors)

answers.answer:
1. Cost 1 Action card plus 1 Ammo; choose Weapon and one Intruder in same Room, discard Ammo, roll combat die.
2. Cost 1 Action card; draw Contamination onto Action discard pile, target Intruder in same Room and roll; any miss causes shooter 1 Serious Wound.
3. Shoot double-hit inflicts 2 Injuries before weapon modifiers; Melee treats double-hit as 1 Injury.
4. Melee draw is not a cost card and cannot pay Actions.
answers.evidence: “Cost 1 Action card plus 1 Ammo; choose Weapon and one Intruder in same Room, discard Ammo, roll combat die.” (Combat)

answers.answer:
1. At 1 Injury Larva dies; remove miniature and no Carcass.
2. Draw 1 Intruder Attack card for Injury Effect, compare blood to total current Injuries; blood ≤ injuries kills Adult, otherwise survives.
3. Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood; sum ≤ current Injuries kills Queen, otherwise survives.
4. Adult/Queen death removes miniature and places Carcass in Room; any Retreat arrow in Queen’s two-card check triggers retreat instead of numeric result (Queen retreats if either arrow).
5. After Queen damage check, draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood; if either shows Retreat arrow, retreat instead: draw Event card, move via Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard Event card.
answers.evidence: “At 1 Injury Larva dies; remove miniature and no Carcass.” (Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat); After Queen damage check, draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood; if either shows Retreat arrow, retreat instead: draw Event card, move via Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard Event card.

answers.answer:
1. Before Escape move, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder, largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.
2. Escape attacks target the escaping Character.
3. If Character dies, their Corpse remains in origin Room and movement does not complete.
4. If survives, move to chosen neighboring explored or unexplored Room; resolve exploration if needed and Noise roll if destination empty.
answers.evidence: “Before Escape move, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder, largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.” (Character Escape)

answers.answer:
1. Among Characters present, target one with fewest Action cards; tie goes to First Player token holder or next in turn order. Surprise Attack instead targets Encounter-triggering Character.
2. For non-Larva draw Attack card: matching Intruder type symbol means resolve card effect; otherwise miss; ignore blood icon and discard card.
3. Draw no Attack card; remove Larva from board and put on target Character board, give target 1 Contamination.
4. Attacking Larva disappears, existing stays, Character gets Contamination but is not automatically killed.
5. Contamination goes atop target’s Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: “Among Characters present, target one with fewest Action cards; tie goes to First Player token holder or next in turn order. Surprise Attack instead targets Encounter-triggering Character.” (Intruder Attack; Infest)

answers.answer:
1. Dressing only suppresses Serious Wound card effect; it still counts, so at 3 Serious Wounds any further Wound kills.
2. Clear Light Wound track and suffer 1 Serious Wound.
3. Remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound as the healing effect specifies.
4. Place Character Corpse Object in death Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: “Dressing only suppresses Serious Wound card effect; it still counts, so at 3 Serious Wounds any further Wound kills.” (Character Wounds and death)

answers.answer:
1. Scan all Contamination cards in hand only; remove non-Infected cards. Infected stays; if no Larva before scan place Larva, if already Larva die and place Creeper in Room.
2. Scan all Contamination cards in deck, hand and discard; remove all Infected cards and remove Larva if present.
3. Then suffer 1 Light Wound, automatically pass, shuffle all cards including entire hand and remaining Contamination into Action deck; hand empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: “Scan all Contamination cards in hand only; remove non-Infected cards. Infected stays; if no Larva before scan place Larva, if already Larva die and place Creeper in Room.” (Contamination; Canteen/Shower; Surgery)

answers.answer:
1. In Room with uncarried Eggs, each Injury destroys one Egg; successful Egg Melee keeps normal Contamination draw, missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound.
2. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; Molotov destroys 1; Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg per Fire Damage step (2 with Vulnerability to Fire).
3. After every single Egg-destruction attempt roll Noise; when no Eggs remain on Intruder board, Nest is destroyed.
4. Summary says manuals do not resolve how missed Egg Melee waiver reconciles with normal pre-roll Contamination draw; no refund or alternate draw timing is specified.
answers.evidence: “In Room with uncarried Eggs, each Injury destroys one Egg; successful Egg Melee keeps normal Contamination draw, missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor Wound.” (Eggs and the Nest)

answers.answer:
1. Pay 2 Action cards for Evacuation Section Room Action; Pod must be unlocked and have free character slot; no entry if Intruder or Malfunction in Section. Roll Noise first; Intruder present or appearing makes attempt fail.
2. Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. After boarding, may launch immediately: remove Pod and occupants from play; they count as arriving on Earth but still face final Contamination and Objective checks.
3. Wait passes current turn and counts as present in Section for bag-development Noise rolls. At start of first round in each later Player Phase choose exactly one: keep waiting/pass, launch, or exit free to Section Room and take full 2-Action round.
4. Second Character boarding may launch both immediately. Intruder appearing in Section returns all Pod occupants to Section Room. Malfunction while waiting still permits wait/launch/exit, but prevents new entry.
answers.evidence: “Pay 2 Action cards for Evacuation Section Room Action; Pod must be unlocked and have free character slot; no entry if Intruder or Malfunction in Section. Roll Noise first; Intruder present or appearing makes attempt fail.” (Escape Pods)

answers.answer:
1. If at least one survivor, check Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives in that order.
2. Two or three Damaged Engines cause ship explosion and everyone aboard, including sleepers, dies; launched Pod passengers are away.
3. Non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters; ship remains undestroyed and Intruders live. Quarantine Objective sleeper survives if destination Mars.
4. Every survivor including Pod passengers is checked: without Larva, scan all Contamination in deck/hand/discard; if none Infected, stop with no four-card draw. If any Infected or Larva present, shuffle all Action/Contamination cards from zones and draw 4; any Contamination among four kills, otherwise survive.
5. Living characters reveal Objective; survival alone is insufficient.
answers.evidence: “If at least one survivor, check Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives in that order.” (Victory Check)

answers.answer:
1. Shuffle all Room 2 tiles face down, place randomly on each slot marked 2, return extras unseen; similarly Room 1 tiles on slots 1. Shuffle Exploration tokens unseen, place one face down each tile, return extras.
2. Place one random Coordinates card face down by Cockpit; Destination marker on B; Time marker on green space.
3. For each Engine shuffle one Working and one Damaged token face down and stack on matching slot (top is true status); put 5 Eggs and 3 random Weakness cards face down on Intruder board.
answers.evidence: “Shuffle all Room 2 tiles face down, place randomly on each slot marked 2, return extras unseen; similarly Room 1 tiles on slots 1. Shuffle Exploration tokens unseen, place one face down each tile, return extras.” (Setup)

answers.answer:
1. Deal numbered Help cards 1 through player count randomly; number also on Inventory sets order and matters to some Objectives.
2. Deal each Corporate and Personal Objective before Character draft; Player 1 draws 2 Character draft cards, reveals both, keeps one and shuffles other back, then others in number order.
3. Each gets Character board/miniature in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10 Action deck, Starting Weapon in Hand with Ammo at capacity, and 2 Quest Items horizontal/inactive. Player 1 gets First Player token; blue Character Corpse token starts Hibernatorium.
4. Not immediately usable; unlock via card mini-quest condition.
answers.evidence: “Deal numbered Help cards 1 through player count randomly; number also on Inventory sets order and matters to some Objectives.” (Crew setup)

answers.answer:
1. At each Player Phase start draw Action cards to hand of 5; after draw pass First Player token left except first game turn.
2. When needing draw with empty Action deck, shuffle discard pile into new deck then draw.
3. Normal discards face up: Action used/discarded to own Action discard; gained Contamination atop it; Item to matching Item discard; Event, Attack, Wound cards to their own discards; discarded markers to pool. Item and other hand cards hidden in Inventory; used Item must be shown.
answers.evidence: “At each Player Phase start draw Action cards to hand of 5; after draw pass First Player token left except first game turn.” (Turn Structure; Discard piles)

answers.answer:
1. Advance Time (and Self-Destruct if active), Intruders attack, Intruders in Fire take 1 Injury/check, resolve Event movement then event effect, then bag development.
2. Only Intruders showing Event card symbol and in a Room with no Characters move through numbered matching Corridor; Technical Corridor result removes Intruder to bag.
3. If Event deck empties, shuffle Event discard into new deck; if Intruder Attack deck empties, shuffle its discard into new deck.
answers.evidence: “Advance Time (and Self-Destruct if active), Intruders attack, Intruders in Fire take 1 Injury/check, resolve Event movement then event effect, then bag development.” (Event Phase)

answers.answer:
1. Bag draw Larva: remove it and add Adult; Creeper: remove it and add Breeder.
2. Adult: return immediately before all non-Combat players roll Noise; Breeder: all non-Combat players roll Noise, then return Breeder.
3. If Character(s) in Nest, place Queen there and resolve Encounter; otherwise add Egg to board (including undiscovered Nest); return Queen.
4. Turn ends only after bag development and any resulting Encounters/attacks fully resolve; then next turn begins.
5. Adult token returns immediately before all players roll Noise in turn order, skipping Characters in Combat; Breeder stays out until all eligible players roll in turn order, then returns. Turn ends only after all bag-development outcomes resolve.
answers.evidence: “Bag draw Larva: remove it and add Adult; Creeper: remove it and add Breeder.” (Intruder bag development); Adult token returns immediately before all players roll Noise in turn order, skipping Characters in Combat; Breeder stays out until all eligible players roll in turn order, then returns. Turn ends only after all bag-development outcomes resolve.

answers.answer:
1. If instructed to place 9th Fire or 9th Malfunction because pool is exhausted, game ends as ship explodes/loses hull. Extra marker when Room already has one does nothing (max 1); removed/discarded markers return pool.
2. All Characters aboard, awake or hibernating, and everything else aboard including Intruders die.
answers.evidence: “If instructed to place 9th Fire or 9th Malfunction because pool is exhausted, game ends as ship explodes/loses hull. Extra marker when Room already has one does nothing (max 1); removed/discarded markers return pool.” (Fire and Malfunction markers)

answers.answer:
1. Malfunction disables that Room Action and Computer; Searching remains usable, and repair effects may discard it.
2. Never in Nest or Slime Room; cannot be placed in unexplored Room; special Room Actions disabled too.
3. Does not change Engine token status. Hibernatorium Malfunction does not harm/wake already-hibernating Character.
answers.evidence: “Malfunction disables that Room Action and Computer; Searching remains usable, and repair effects may discard it.” (Malfunction markers)

answers.answer:
1. Normal Item cards are hidden in Inventory, others see backs/colors; no Inventory size limit; reveal any Item when used.
2. Heavy Items/Objects are public and occupy one of two Hand slots; max 2 carried. Heavy Items found in Search need no separate Pick Up Action; Weapons found by Search have 1 Ammo.
3. Add-type items attach to another card as one; Duct Tape combines 2 Heavy Items in one slot, never Objects.
answers.evidence: “Normal Item cards are hidden in Inventory, others see backs/colors; no Inventory size limit; reveal any Item when used.” (Items and Objects)

answers.answer:
1. Drop free any time during your turn, no Action; dropped Objects stay in Room; dropped Items are lost/discarded.
2. Found Weapons start with 1 Ammo; Starting Weapon is loaded to printed Ammo capacity. Never above capacity.
answers.evidence: “Drop free any time during your turn, no Action; dropped Objects stay in Room; dropped Items are lost/discarded.” (Items and Objects)

answers.answer:
1. Search chooses matching color deck (Room background); white Room allows any Red/Yellow/Green deck; draw 2, keep 1 and return other face down to bottom of chosen deck.
2. Each Search reduces Item Counter by 1; at zero Room emptied and cannot be searched, except Scout Scavenging.
3. Nest and Slime Room prohibit Search; Special Rooms have no Searching; Blue Crafted Items never found through Search.
answers.evidence: “Search chooses matching color deck (Room background); white Room allows any Red/Yellow/Green deck; draw 2, keep 1 and return other face down to bottom of chosen deck.” (Searching)

answers.answer:
1. Craft Basic Action costs its Action card and 2 Item cards whose blue component icons match Crafted card gray icons.
2. Result card must be available; players may inspect Craft deck anytime.
3. Antidote flame + medical cross; Taser battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov flame + folded cloth/fabric.
answers.evidence: “Craft Basic Action costs its Action card and 2 Item cards whose blue component icons match Crafted card gray icons.” (Crafting)

answers.answer:
1. Only Trade initiator spends Action; all Characters in Room may exchange among themselves if mutually agreed.
2. May give Item/Object for nothing; cannot exchange Ammo.
3. No separate pickup Action: Search already gains Heavy Item.
answers.evidence: “Only Trade initiator spends Action; all Characters in Room may exchange among themselves if mutually agreed.” (Trade)

answers.answer:
1. Laboratory Analyse requires corresponding Object present in Laboratory: Corpse, Egg, or Carcass corresponds to its Weakness card.
2. Reveal corresponding Weakness face up; leave on Intruder board; Object is not consumed and Weakness benefits all players.
3. Discover Weakness Objective requires someone to research corresponding Object before game end, not necessarily you.
4. Corpse corresponds to Corpse Weakness, Egg to Egg Weakness, and Intruder Carcass to Carcass Weakness; object itself must be present in Laboratory.
answers.evidence: “Laboratory Analyse requires corresponding Object present in Laboratory: Corpse, Egg, or Carcass corresponds to its Weakness card.” (Objective types; Laboratory); Corpse corresponds to Corpse Weakness, Egg to Egg Weakness, and Intruder Carcass to Carcass Weakness; object itself must be present in Laboratory.

answers.answer:
1. Room Action costs 2 Action cards; must be in Room, not in Combat, and Room has no Malfunction.
2. Computer icon itself does not create an effect; it enables relevant card abilities. Fire does not disable Room Actions or Search; ending round there wounds Character.
answers.evidence: “Room Action costs 2 Action cards; must be in Room, not in Combat, and Room has no Malfunction.” (Room Actions)

answers.answer: 1. Costs normal Room Action 2 cards; add 2 Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons, never Classic Weapons and never beyond capacity.
answers.evidence: “Costs normal Room Action 2 cards; add 2 Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons, never Classic Weapons and never beyond capacity.” (Room Actions: Armory)

answers.answer:
1. Choose exactly one: dress all Serious Wounds; heal one Dressed Serious Wound; or heal all Light Wounds.
2. Dressing flips card face down and suppresses effect but wound still counts. Duplicate Serious Wound effects do not stack cumulatively.
answers.evidence: “Choose exactly one: dress all Serious Wounds; heal one Dressed Serious Wound; or heal all Light Wounds.” (Emergency Room; Character Wounds)

answers.answer:
1. Comms Room Action places Status marker on your Character board Signal space; it is only used for Objectives.
2. Comms Room is always aboard in normal game.
answers.evidence: “Comms Room Action places Status marker on your Character board Signal space; it is only used for Objectives.” (Room Actions: Comms Room)

answers.answer: 1. Choose any one Room; discard Fire marker there if present and make all Intruders there run away in random directions, drawing one Event card per Intruder. Works even if chosen Room has no Fire.
answers.evidence: “Choose any one Room; discard Fire marker there if present and make all Intruders there run away in random directions, drawing one Event card per Intruder. Works even if chosen Room has no Fire.” (Room Actions: Fire Control System)

answers.answer:
1. Generator starts Self-Destruct at first green track space; Character may stop it by removing marker until point of no return, and new sequence restarts at green. Advance one each Time advance.
2. First yellow makes sequence unabortable and unlocks Pods; they can be relocked, but later yellow spaces do not unlock again. Final skull space explodes ship.
3. Hyperspace jump while sequence active still counts ship destroyed. Character cannot initiate while anyone hibernates; Coolant Leak Event may start it despite sleepers.
answers.evidence: “Generator starts Self-Destruct at first green track space; Character may stop it by removing marker until point of no return, and new sequence restarts at green. Advance one each Time advance.” (Self-Destruct sequence)

answers.answer:
1. Airlock Control chooses any one other Yellow Room whose connected Corridors have no Destroyed Doors; automatically closes every Door around target and places Procedure token.
2. If all doors remain closed through end of current Player Phase (all passed), everything in Room dies and Fire removed; opening any Door first cancels procedure.
answers.evidence: “Airlock Control chooses any one other Yellow Room whose connected Corridors have no Destroyed Doors; automatically closes every Door around target and places Procedure token.” (Room Actions: Airlock Control)

answers.answer:
1. At start of new turn, Character in Cabins with no Intruders draws 1 extra Action card, hand size 6.
2. Malfunction disables effect. Passive, not paid Room Action.
answers.evidence: “At start of new turn, Character in Cabins with no Intruders draws 1 extra Action card, hand size 6.” (Room Actions: Cabins)

answers.answer: 1. As Room Action choose any Room, including distant; open or close any chosen subset of Doors in its connected Corridors. Destroyed Doors cannot be closed again (unless Plasma Torch); summary does not specify Command Center can restore them.
answers.evidence: “As Room Action choose any Room, including distant; open or close any chosen subset of Doors in its connected Corridors. Destroyed Doors cannot be closed again (unless Plasma Torch); summary does not specify Command Center can restore them.” (Room Actions: Command Center)

answers.answer:
1. Can check status of all 3 Engines; cannot change Engine status.
2. Check works even if an Engine Room has Malfunction.
answers.evidence: “Can check status of all 3 Engines; cannot change Engine status.” (Room Actions: Engine Control Room)

answers.answer:
1. Flip one Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked.
2. Secretly inspect any one unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replace them; may lie about what saw.
answers.evidence: “Flip one Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked.” (Room Actions: Hatch Control System; Monitoring Room)

answers.answer:
1. No Action: entering Room Covered With Slime automatically gives Slime before token resolution.
2. No Item Counter and Malfunction can never be placed there; Slime max one, further Slime no effect.
3. Shower removes Slime but does not remove Fire.
answers.evidence: “No Action: entering Room Covered With Slime automatically gives Slime before token resolution.” (Room Covered With Slime; Shower Room)

answers.answer:
1. Check Coordinates secretly look at Coordinates card and may lie, replacing it and remembering; Set Destination moves marker.
2. Marker selects one of four entries on Coordinates card. Cannot set with Intruder in Cockpit or change after any Character hibernates.
3. Check Coordinates is secret: look at card, replace it, and may lie about what you saw. Set Destination moves the marker, which selects one of four entries on the Coordinates card; cannot set with Intruder in Cockpit or change after anyone hibernates.
answers.evidence: “Check Coordinates secretly look at Coordinates card and may lie, replacing it and remembering; Set Destination moves marker.” (Cockpit); Check Coordinates is secret: look at card, replace it, and may lie about what you saw. Set Destination moves the marker, which selects one of four entries on the Coordinates card; cannot set with Intruder in Cockpit or change after anyone hibernates.

answers.answer:
1. Check in Engine Room secretly view top Engine token, may lie. Repair/Break via Repairs Action or Tools Item secretly examine both tokens and restack in any order.
2. Need not say whether repaired, but must announce if token order changed.
3. No prior check or functioning Engine Room required; works with Malfunction.
answers.evidence: “Check in Engine Room secretly view top Engine token, may lie. Repair/Break via Repairs Action or Tools Item secretly examine both tokens and restack in any order.” (Engines)

answers.answer:
1. Only when Time marker blue, pay 2 Action cards, be in Hibernatorium with no Intruder/Malfunction; roll Noise; Intruder reaching/appearing makes attempt fail.
2. Otherwise remove miniature and stop participating until end checks.
3. Once anyone hibernates, Characters may neither change Destination nor initiate Self-Destruct; Coolant Leak Event exception. Later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake/harm sleeper.
answers.evidence: “Only when Time marker blue, pay 2 Action cards, be in Hibernatorium with no Intruder/Malfunction; roll Noise; Intruder reaching/appearing makes attempt fail.” (Hibernatorium)

answers.answer:
1. Time reaches final red: immediate jump; awake Characters aboard die from g-force, hibernators do not die from jump; Intruders unharmed.
2. When last alive nonhibernating Character dies, hibernates or launches, if Self-Destruct active move its marker to final space; otherwise Time to final space, resolve corresponding effects.
3. Intruders survive normal jump; active Self-Destruct means ship destroyed at jump.
answers.evidence: “Time reaches final red: immediate jump; awake Characters aboard die from g-force, hibernators do not die from jump; Intruders unharmed.” (End of the game)

answers.answer:
1. Characters cannot directly attack other Characters (anti-aggression implants).
2. Actions/effects can harm indirectly, e.g. lock someone in burning Room, start Self-Destruct with crew aboard, throw Grenade into occupied Room.
answers.evidence: “Characters cannot directly attack other Characters (anti-aggression implants).” (Attacking other players)

answers.answer:
1. If placing Adult with all 8 models on board, remove all Adult models not in Combat and return their tokens to bag if possible, then place Adult in Encounter Room. If all eight Adults are in Combat, summary explicitly says procedure unresolved; authoritative clarification needed.
2. Intruder ending movement in unexplored Room does not reveal Room/token and remains there.
answers.evidence: “If placing Adult with all 8 models on board, remove all Adult models not in Combat and return their tokens to bag if possible, then place Adult in Encounter Room. If all eight Adults are in Combat, summary explicitly says procedure unresolved; authoritative clarification needed.” (Adult overflow; Intruders in unexplored Rooms)

answers.answer:
1. Shoot: 1 Injury only Larva/Creeper, otherwise miss. Melee same restriction; ineligible target means miss and shooter takes Serious Wound.
2. Shoot: 1 Injury Larva/Creeper/Adult, miss Breeder/Queen. Melee same restriction and miss against ineligible target causes Serious Wound.
answers.evidence: “Shoot: 1 Injury only Larva/Creeper, otherwise miss. Melee same restriction; ineligible target means miss and shooter takes Serious Wound.” (Combat die results)

requested_parts: no Larva and all scan clean
answers.answer:
1. Scan all Contamination in deck/hand/discard; if none Infected, no four-card draw and scanned non-Infected cards are not removed by endgame check.
2. Earlier launched passengers still undergo final Contamination and Objective checks.
answers.evidence: “Scan all Contamination in deck/hand/discard; if none Infected, no four-card draw and scanned non-Infected cards are not removed by endgame check.” (Victory Check: Contamination)

answers.answer: 1. Antidote: flame + medical cross; Taser: battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower: flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail: flame + folded cloth/fabric.
answers.evidence: “Antidote: flame + medical cross; Taser: battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower: flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail: flame + folded cloth/fabric.” (Crafting)

answers.answer:
1. In Combat whenever Intruder shares Room with Character; Eggs do not count.
2. In Combat Only and Out of Combat Only restrictions must be followed; unmarked card and Item Actions may be used in either if requirements met. Basic Actions in Combat only Shoot, Melee, and Movement as Escape; Room Actions forbidden.
answers.evidence: “In Combat whenever Intruder shares Room with Character; Eggs do not count.” (Combat rules)

answers.answer:
1. Target Character must be dead at game end; you need not personally kill them. Hibernating or escaped Character counts as surviving, not dead.
2. No other Character may survive.
3. Regardless of Objective, your Character must survive by Pod or hibernation.
answers.evidence: “Target Character must be dead at game end; you need not personally kill them. Hibernating or escaped Character counts as surviving, not dead.” (Objective types; Winning)

answers.answer:
1. If Door token needed but pool empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on board.
2. Open is no token; Closed standing token; Destroyed lying token, movement allowed and cannot close again except Plasma Torch. Max one per Corridor; never place in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: “If Door token needed but pool empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on board.” (Door tokens)

answers.answer:
1. All Escape Pods automatically unlock immediately on first Character death.
2. For rest of game they may be Locked or Unlocked normally, e.g. Hatch Control; may relock.
answers.evidence: “All Escape Pods automatically unlock immediately on first Character death.” (First dead Character)

answers.answer:
1. Room Action draws 2 cards from chosen Red/Yellow/Green Item deck, keep 1 and return other face down to bottom of that deck.
2. Costs 2 Action cards, require presence in Room, no Combat and no Malfunction.
answers.evidence: “Room Action draws 2 cards from chosen Red/Yellow/Green Item deck, keep 1 and return other face down to bottom of that deck.” (Storage)

answers.answer:
1. Use Nest Room Action: pay 2 Action cards, take 1 Egg token from Intruder board, then roll Noise.
2. A previously taken/dropped Egg in Room is an Object picked up via Basic Pick Up Heavy Object cost 1 Action card; no Nest Action/Noise instruction. Removing from board reduces Nest Eggs; dropping back does not restore total.
answers.evidence: “Use Nest Room Action: pay 2 Action cards, take 1 Egg token from Intruder board, then roll Noise.” (Nest; Pick Up Heavy Object)

answers.answer: 1. Pay printed Action-card cost and show Item when used; discard One Use Only Item after use.
answers.evidence: “Pay printed Action-card cost and show Item when used; discard One Use Only Item after use.” (Actions from Item cards)

answers.answer:
1. Launched Pod occupants count as arriving on Earth.
2. This only defines Character arrival; ship’s own destination/Coordinates and Engine check remain separate and are not proven Earth-bound by Pod launch.
answers.evidence: “Launched Pod occupants count as arriving on Earth.” (Escape Pods)

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Waiting Pod occupants are treated as present in Section for bag-development Noise rolls; Adult development calls all eligible non-Combat players to roll.
answers.evidence: “Yes. Waiting Pod occupants are treated as present in Section for bag-development Noise rolls; Adult development calls all eligible non-Combat players to roll.” (Escape Pods)

answers.answer:
1. May continue waiting, launch or exit into Section Room; Malfunction does not remove those options.
2. It blocks only new entry to Pods in that Section.
answers.evidence: “May continue waiting, launch or exit into Section Room; Malfunction does not remove those options.” (Escape Pods)

answers.answer: 1. Resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder present, in size order largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.
answers.evidence: “Resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder present, in size order largest first: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.” (Character Escape)

answers.answer: 1. Yes. FAQ says remove Event from game even when its other effect cannot resolve.
answers.evidence: “Yes. FAQ says remove Event from game even when its other effect cannot resolve.” (FAQ: Events)

answers.answer:
1. In bag development return drawn Adult token to bag immediately before all eligible players roll Noise.
2. Yes; Encounter from a roll may draw that same Adult token.
answers.evidence: “In bag development return drawn Adult token to bag immediately before all eligible players roll Noise.” (Intruder bag development)

answers.answer:
1. Retreating Intruder meeting Closed Door destroys Door and stays in place.
2. Under The Way of Moving, affected Intruder other than Breeder/Queen instead does nothing at that Door.
answers.evidence: “Retreating Intruder meeting Closed Door destroys Door and stays in place.” (FAQ: Intruder Retreat)

answers.answer: 1. No. Hand Serious Wound raises Item Action costs; Basic Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action.
answers.evidence: “No. Hand Serious Wound raises Item Action costs; Basic Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action.” (FAQ: Actions and character abilities)

answers.answer: 1. Adds 1 Injury per damage instance (x+1). Flamethrower double-crosshair hit deals 3 Injuries.
answers.evidence: “Adds 1 Injury per damage instance (x+1). Flamethrower double-crosshair hit deals 3 Injuries.” (FAQ: Vulnerability to Fire)

answers.answer: 1. Attacking Larva is removed/disappears; existing Larva stays on Character board; Character gains 1 Contamination and is not automatically killed by this duplicate-Larva attack.
answers.evidence: “Attacking Larva is removed/disappears; existing Larva stays on Character board; Character gains 1 Contamination and is not automatically killed by this duplicate-Larva attack.” (Infest)

answers.answer:
1. Hibernated Character takes no later Fire wounds in Hibernatorium.
2. Ship destruction/endgame checks may still kill them (e.g. explosion or applicable survival checks).
answers.evidence: “Hibernated Character takes no later Fire wounds in Hibernatorium.” (FAQ: Hibernation)

answers.answer:
1. Yes, Coolant Leak Event can start Self-Destruct while someone hibernates.
2. Characters themselves cannot start Self-Destruct if anyone hibernating.
answers.evidence: “Yes, Coolant Leak Event can start Self-Destruct while someone hibernates.” (Self-Destruct sequence)

answers.answer: 1. Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to unused token pool, not permanently removed; reusable later.
answers.evidence: “Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to unused token pool, not permanently removed; reusable later.” (FAQ: Intruder tokens)

answers.answer: 1. Fire may be placed in unexplored Rooms; Malfunction may not.
answers.evidence: “Fire may be placed in unexplored Rooms; Malfunction may not.” (Malfunction markers)

answers.answer: 1. First Light Wound fills second Light slot; next Light converts 3-Light track to 1 Serious Wound; fourth incoming Light then remains as 1 Light Wound. Result: 1 Serious and 1 Light.
answers.evidence: “First Light Wound fills second Light slot; next Light converts 3-Light track to 1 Serious Wound; fourth incoming Light then remains as 1 Light Wound. Result: 1 Serious and 1 Light.” (FAQ: Character wounds)

answers.answer: 1. Heavy Objects drop in death Room; Item cards disappear from game.
answers.evidence: “Heavy Objects drop in death Room; Item cards disappear from game.” (FAQ: Character death)

answers.answer: 1. No. Pods automatically unlock only when Self-Destruct first reaches a yellow space; later yellow spaces do not unlock them again after relocking.
answers.evidence: “No. Pods automatically unlock only when Self-Destruct first reaches a yellow space; later yellow spaces do not unlock them again after relocking.” (Self-Destruct sequence)

answers.answer:
1. Ship destruction fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements because everything aboard dies.
2. Not sufficient alone: your Character must also survive and fulfill all Objective requirements.
answers.evidence: “Ship destruction fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements because everything aboard dies.” (FAQ: Objectives)

answers.answer:
1. No intentional empty Action with no meaningful game-state change; starting Trade with no intent to exchange is disallowed.
2. If genuine negotiations end without trade, that is allowed.
answers.evidence: “No intentional empty Action with no meaningful game-state change; starting Trade with no intent to exchange is disallowed.” (FAQ: Trade)

answers.answer:
1. Quest Item activation is Basic Action printed on its card; forbidden in Combat.
2. Allowed in a Malfunctioning Room; Room Malfunction does not block this Basic Action.
answers.evidence: “Quest Item activation is Basic Action printed on its card; forbidden in Combat.” (FAQ: Quest activation)

answers.answer:
1. Only Shoot, Melee Attack, and Basic Movement as Escape.
2. Cannot Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object/Object, or activate Quest Item in Combat.
3. Unmarked Actions from cards or Items are allowed in either state if requirements met; tagged restrictions still apply.
answers.evidence: “Only Shoot, Melee Attack, and Basic Movement as Escape.” (Actions; Combat)

answers.answer:
1. Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone; both Characters move in directions of their choice.
2. Perform one Noise roll for the two movers; any Encounter compares Surprise against Soldier.
answers.evidence: “Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone; both Characters move in directions of their choice.” (FAQ: Covering Fire)

answers.answer: 1. Remove all Ammo and perform one Shoot Action; damage equals Shoot die result plus half discarded Ammo rounded down plus Assault Rifle +1 bonus.
answers.evidence: “Remove all Ammo and perform one Shoot Action; damage equals Shoot die result plus half discarded Ammo rounded down plus Assault Rifle +1 bonus.” (FAQ: Full Auto)

answers.answer: 1. May see Intruder Attack card before choosing Nerves of Steel. It can protect Soldier even when another Character triggered Surprise Attack; only Soldier benefits, other characters still resolve effects such as Frenzy.
answers.evidence: “May see Intruder Attack card before choosing Nerves of Steel. It can protect Soldier even when another Character triggered Surprise Attack; only Soldier benefits, other characters still resolve effects such as Frenzy.” (FAQ: Nerves of Steel)

answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration result with chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic Exploration results too.
answers.evidence: “Careful Movement replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration result with chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic Exploration results too.” (FAQ: Careful Movement; Reconnaissance)

answers.answer:
1. Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat.
2. Intercom can cause another Character to Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape rules including attacks and destination effects.
answers.evidence: “Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat.” (FAQ: Captain abilities)

answers.answer:
1. With active Intercom, Motivation affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain’s Room.
2. With active Intercom, Motivation’s Action-card draw effect reaches Characters in Captain’s Room and Characters in any Room with a Computer.
answers.evidence: “With active Intercom, Motivation affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain’s Room.” (FAQ: Motivation); With active Intercom, Motivation’s Action-card draw effect reaches Characters in Captain’s Room and Characters in any Room with a Computer.

answers.answer: 1. Door Exploration token is ignored when entering by Technical Corridors Action or Plans Item, because entry Corridor cannot be determined; no Door placed.
answers.evidence: “Door Exploration token is ignored when entering by Technical Corridors Action or Plans Item, because entry Corridor cannot be determined; no Door placed.” (FAQ: Technical Corridors)

answers.answer:
1. Cannot Interrupt remote Captain Order via Intercom if you are not in same Room as Character performing interrupted Action.
2. Passing does not bar Interruption; FAQ permits it after pass, subject to same-Room requirement.
answers.evidence: “Cannot Interrupt remote Captain Order via Intercom if you are not in same Room as Character performing interrupted Action.” (FAQ: Interruption)

answers.answer:
1. After two Actions empty hand does not automatically force pass; wait until next round to pass.
2. That extra round may trigger another Fire or Bleeding effect.
answers.evidence: “After two Actions empty hand does not automatically force pass; wait until next round to pass.” (FAQ: Rounds)

answers.answer:
1. If no Larva before Rest, multiple Infected cards place only one Larva and do not themselves kill.
2. Rest can be fatal if Larva already on board before its scan.
answers.evidence: “If no Larva before Rest, multiple Infected cards place only one Larva and do not themselves kill.” (FAQ: Rest)

answers.answer: 1. When throwing Grenade/Molotov at Nest Eggs from neighboring Room, required Noise roll is in thrower’s own Room.
answers.evidence: “When throwing Grenade/Molotov at Nest Eggs from neighboring Room, required Noise roll is in thrower’s own Room.” (FAQ: Eggs)

answers.answer: 1. No. Intranet/Scientist location does not waive research requirement: Object itself must be in Laboratory to Analyse/reveal Weakness.
answers.evidence: “No. Intranet/Scientist location does not waive research requirement: Object itself must be in Laboratory to Analyse/reveal Weakness.” (FAQ: Intranet research)

answers.answer:
1. Storage Room Action remains usable repeatedly at zero counter, paying normal cost/restrictions.
2. Item Counter limits Search Action card; at zero ordinary Search unavailable (except Scout Scavenging).
answers.evidence: “Storage Room Action remains usable repeatedly at zero counter, paying normal cost/restrictions.” (FAQ: Storage)

answers.answer: 1. Vulnerability to Fire adds one Injury per damage instance; burning Nest destroys 2 Eggs each Fire Damage step.
answers.evidence: “Vulnerability to Fire adds one Injury per damage instance; burning Nest destroys 2 Eggs each Fire Damage step.” (FAQ: Fire and Eggs)

answers.answer: 1. No. Once removed from Intruder board, Egg token is a normal Heavy Object; dropping it in Nest does not restore board Egg total/hit points.
answers.evidence: “No. Once removed from Intruder board, Egg token is a normal Heavy Object; dropping it in Nest does not restore board Egg total/hit points.” (FAQ: Eggs)

answers.answer: 1. Each affected target’s player chooses and discards 1 Action card from their own hand.
answers.evidence: “Each affected target’s player chooses and discards 1 Action card from their own hand.” (FAQ: Smoke Grenade)

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters.
answers.evidence: “Yes. Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters.” (FAQ: Items)

answers.answer: 1. Cannot directly use Charge to reload another Character’s Weapon. Trade Charge to them so they use it in their own round.
answers.evidence: “Cannot directly use Charge to reload another Character’s Weapon. Trade Charge to them so they use it in their own round.” (FAQ: Energy Charge)

answers.answer: 1. Does not place Larva for Infected result; instead gain a new Contamination card.
answers.evidence: “Does not place Larva for Infected result; instead gain a new Contamination card.” (FAQ: Alcohol)

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to used/empty Energy Weapon immediately provides its extra Ammo.
answers.evidence: “Yes. Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to used/empty Energy Weapon immediately provides its extra Ammo.” (FAQ: Added Items)

answers.answer: 1. Starts fully loaded, not with one Ammo as a Weapon found by Search.
answers.evidence: “Starts fully loaded, not with one Ammo as a Weapon found by Search.” (FAQ: Crafted Flamethrower)

answers.answer: 1. No. Hand Serious Wound does not affect Scout’s Motion Scanner because it is a unique reaction, not an Item Action.
answers.evidence: “No. Hand Serious Wound does not affect Scout’s Motion Scanner because it is a unique reaction, not an Item Action.” (FAQ: Motion Scanner)

answers.answer:
1. Scan all own Contamination in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from game.
2. Gain 1 new Contamination, then reshuffle it with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in hand.
3. Then pass; may keep hand cards.
4. Surgery scans same zones and removes infected cards, removes Larva if present, gives no new Contamination, suffers 1 Light Wound, then automatically passes and shuffles entire hand plus remaining cards into Action deck (empty hand).
answers.evidence: “Scan all own Contamination in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from game.” (FAQ: Antidote; Surgery)

answers.answer: 1. Exploration Slime places Status marker on Character board; Fire and Malfunction markers in entered Room; Door token in Corridor by which Character entered.
answers.evidence: “Exploration Slime places Status marker on Character board; Fire and Malfunction markers in entered Room; Door token in Corridor by which Character entered.” (Exploration tokens)

answers.answer: 1. After Intruder Attacks and before Event card, each Intruder in burning Room takes 1 Injury; immediately apply normal Injury Effect check, including death or retreat.
answers.evidence: “After Intruder Attacks and before Event card, each Intruder in burning Room takes 1 Injury; immediately apply normal Injury Effect check, including death or retreat.” (Event Phase Fire Damage)

answers.answer: 1. No. Nest and Room Covered With Slime explicitly prohibit any Search Action, even though ordinary searchable Rooms allow it.
answers.evidence: “No. Nest and Room Covered With Slime explicitly prohibit any Search Action, even though ordinary searchable Rooms allow it.” (Searching)

answers.answer:
1. On ordinary Movement into Slime Room, first gain Slime, then reveal/resolve Exploration Silence; because now slimed, Silence becomes Danger.
2. Move all neighboring Intruders not in Combat into this Room; if none eligible, place Noise in every connected unmarked Corridor, including Technical if entrance.
3. No separate normal Noise roll because Exploration token resolves Silence/Danger instead. After resolution remove Exploration token from game into box.
answers.evidence: “On ordinary Movement into Slime Room, first gain Slime, then reveal/resolve Exploration Silence; because now slimed, Silence becomes Danger.” (Room Covered With Slime; Exploration tokens; Noise roll)
